test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

A misunderstanding has crept between he and his sister.
solution:
The correct answer is **'****between he****'**, i.e. the error lies in this part of the sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the incorrect usage of the subjective pronoun 'he'.
 
• In the given sentence, **'between'** is used as a **preposition**, and **a preposition is always followed by an objective case pronoun.**
 
• Example: 
 
 
• It is between **him** and me.
 
• Everyone but **him **attended the meeting.
 
 
 
• ​Thus, 'him' will be used in place of 'he'.

 

Correct sentence: __*A misunderstanding has crept **between __him__** and his sister.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• Pronouns: a word that can function by itself as a noun phrase and that refers either to the participants in the discourse or to someone or something mentioned elsewhere in the discourse.
 
• **Subjective case pronoun: **The subjective (or nominative) pronouns are I, you (singular), he/she/it, we, you (plural), they and who. A subjective pronoun acts as a subject in a sentence.
 
• **Objective case pronoun**: The objective (or accusative) case pronouns are me, you (singular), him/her/it, us, you (plural), them and whom. The objective case is used when something is being done to (or given to, etc.) someone.
